exact_target: For an n-by-n iid uniform {−1,+1} matrix B, show that there exists an absolute q in (0,1) such that P(s_min(B) <= epsilon/sqrt(n)) <= epsilon + q^n for every epsilon >= 0 and all sufficiently large n.

original_primary_source.title: Smoothed analysis of algorithms
original_primary_source.authors: Daniel A. Spielman and Shang-Hua Teng
original_primary_source.location: page 8, Conjecture 2, lines 610-632 in web extraction
original_primary_source.form: P(||A^{-1}|| > t) <= sqrt(d)/t + alpha^n for a d-by-d iid sign matrix and an absolute alpha<1; original printed n in the exponential despite using d for dimension.
original_primary_source.normalization_note: With t=sqrt(d)/epsilon and ||A^{-1}||=1/s_min(A), this is the least-singular-value formulation; its strict threshold implies the non-strict version by continuity from above when the bound holds for every t. Interpret inverse norm as infinity on singular matrices.

later_primary_source.title: On the Spielman-Teng Conjecture
later_primary_source.authors: Ashwin Sah, Julian Sahasrabudhe, Mehtaab Sawhney
later_primary_source.result: For iid mean-zero, variance-one subgaussian entries, P(s_min(M) <= epsilon/sqrt(n)) <= (1+o(1))epsilon + exp(-Omega(n)), with stated o(1)=O((log n)^(-1/16)); the exact coefficient one is not proved by that theorem.

prior_attempt_correction: C0029-A001 describes 1-exp(-t^2/2-t) as an exact finite-n Gaussian CDF; it is a limiting law. Already at n=1 and t=1, the exact CDF is erf(1/sqrt(2))=0.6826894921, while the asserted expression is 0.7768698399.
local_previous_work: Scoped rg found no C0029 or Spielman-Teng hits in the H and I attempt markdown/jsonl files or the Team O board. This is a bounded negative search, not a proof of absence.
current_openness_reason: The 2025 primary paper stops at 1+o(1); bounded web and local searches did not verify whether a later exact-coefficient result exists. No novelty claim is made.
